summary: Nyoten Jinbo (1880–1946) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Baisen Azegami. He held a professorship at Komazawa University.

Odette Viennot (1910–1992) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. Educated at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and École du Louvre, she studied under Philippe Stern, held a post at the Guimet Museum, and worked at the CNRS (~1949–1978).
Odolen Smékal (1928–1998) was an Indologist and linguist. He earned his Ph.D. at Charles University in 1952 studying under Vincenc Pořízka, and taught Hindi there starting in 1954.
Ofer Peres is an Indology and religious studies scholar who held posts at Heidelberg University's South Asia Institute and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (attested 2016–2026).

Ogyen Trinley Dorje (born 1985) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure. He studied under teachers including Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche, the 14th Dalai Lama, and Bokar Rinpoche, and taught Khenpo Sherab Püntsok.
Ohryu Matsushima is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (attested 2003) and held a post there.

Oktiabrina Volkova (1926–1988) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg State University and under Bidia Dandaron. She taught at MGIMO (1952–1956) and served as a researcher at the Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies (1956–1981).

Olaf Hansen (1902–1969), an Iranian and Central Asian studies linguist, earned his Ph.D. under Hans Reichelt and completed his Habilitation at the University of Hamburg. He served as Professor of Indo-Iranian at the Free University of Berlin (1950–1968).

Olav Hackstein (born 1962) specializes in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Freiburg and the University of Pennsylvania, and became a professor at the University of Munich in 2008.

Oldřich Friš (1903–1955) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Charles University under Vincenc Lesný. He held posts at Palacký University Olomouc and Charles University, where he directed the Section of Near and Middle Eastern and Indian Languages.

Oldřich Hujer (1880–1942) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Charles University under Josef Zubatý and at Leipzig University. He served as ordinary Professor of Comparative Indo-European Linguistics at Charles University from 1924 to 1942.

Ole Holten Pind (1945–2018) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed his doctorate at the University of Vienna under Ernst Steinkellner and held a professorship at the University of Hamburg.

Oleg Grabar (1929–2011) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at the University of Paris, Harvard, and Princeton, he held professorships at the University of Michigan, Harvard University, and the Institute for Advanced Study.
Olga Nowicka is an Indologist who held a post at Jagiellonian University (attested 2018) and was a Ph.D. candidate there (attested 2020).
Olha Dobrodum works in Indology and religious studies. She studied at Odesa University in 2015 and held a post at the State University of Trade and Economics.

Oliver Codrington (1837–1921), active in history, archaeology, and Indology, studied at London Hospital. He served in the Army Medical Department (1859–1885), was Secretary of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai, and was Librarian of the Royal Asiatic Society.
Oliver Freiberger is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He held posts at the University of Bayreuth (attested 1996) and the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2026).

Oliver Hector de Alwis Wijesekera (1909–1990) specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Ceylon and earned a Ph.D. at SOAS under William Stede, later heading the Sanskrit department at the University of Ceylon.

Oliver Hellwig is an Indologist and computational linguist who completed his habilitation under Harry Falk. He has held academic posts at Heidelberg University, the University of Düsseldorf, and the University of Zurich.
Oliver Petersen (born 1961) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Geshe Thubten Ngawang and held a post at Tibetisches Zentrum Hamburg (attested 2002).
